## Description

Let's start by showing random dog pictures on the website! To do that, fetch a dog picture when a user clicks on the button and show the picture.

In this project, use the [DOG API](https://dog.ceo/dog-api/documentation). Take a look at the documentation; you will use the different endpoints.

This stage requires a random image endpoint, so check it out! Take a look at the JSON response object sample as well; it should give you an idea of how to display the data.

Before starting with the JavaScript part, let's put some HTML elements on the page.

First, put a first-level `header` that says `Dog Glossary`, so we know where we are. Second, add a `button` with the id of `button-random-dog` with the text `Show Random Dog`. You may have noticed that this button triggers a request to the API to obtain the data. Lastly, you need a place to display the data ÔÇö create a `div` with the id of `content`.

Once the page is set up, the functionality is as follows:

- After clicking on the `Show Random Dog` button, you should get a random picture from the API and display it as an image on the page;
- The image should be in the `content` div. After clicking on the button again, it must replace the old image with a new one, instead of showing two images.

You can use the IDs we've provided to select the elements.

## Objectives

Your page should:

- Contain a first-level `header` with the text `Dog Glossary`;
- Contain a `button` with the id of `button-random-dog` and the text `Show Random Dog`;
- Contain a `div` with the id of `content`;
- Use the [DOG API](https://dog.ceo/dog-api/documentation);
- Display a random image from the API after clicking on the `Show Random Dog`.

## Example

**Example 1**: *after clicking the button.*

![Layout of the Dog Glossary website](https://ucarecdn.com/749bf24e-4df2-41e1-91b4-31f0eb5bf2de/)
title: Random dog

## Description

Now, we will get the breed name from the user and show a picture of that breed instead of a random breed.

Look at the endpoints in the API documentation again and notice the one where we can enter different breed names and get a picture.

Add `input` with the ID of `input-breed` and the placeholder of `Enter a breed`. Optionally, add a `label` too, but the tests won't check it.

Also, add the `button` with the id of `button-show-breed` and the text `Show Breed`.

The functionality part should be similar to the previous stage, except for a few additions:

- This time you will get the breed name from the input and use that to get a response. Make sure to handle both upper- or lower-cased inputs;
- Make sure to have at most one item inside the `content` div;
- Another case to handle is when users enter an unknown input, show a paragraph that says `Breed not found!` instead of an image.

You can use the IDs we've provided to select the elements.

## Objectives

Your page should:

- Contain `input` with the ID of `input-breed` and the placeholder `Enter a breed`;
- Contain a `button` with the ID of `button-show-breed` and the text `Show Breed`;
- Use the [DOG API](https://dog.ceo/dog-api/documentation);
- Display the input breed's image from the API;
- Handle an unknown input and show a paragraph with the text `Breed not found!`

## Examples

**Example 1:** *Enter a breed name and click the button*

![Dog Glossary: Enter a breed name and click the button](https://ucarecdn.com/2abc2571-9501-4b7c-ad4c-0b81233e21fb/)

**Example 2**: *after entering an unknown breed name and clicking the button*

![Dog Glossary: After entering an unknown breed name and clicking the button](https://ucarecdn.com/8742c573-33c5-4b18-b918-6b03b93e4bea/)

## Description

So far, we've shown random images and requested images for cute dog breeds on the Internet. Now, let's show sub-breeds of a specific breed.

Similar to the previous stage, when users enter a breed name, show sub-breeds using the API. You can check the documentation to see the endpoint.

Start by adding a new `button` with the ID `button-show-sub-breed` and the text `Show Sub-Breed`.

Use the same `input` tag from the previous stage to get the user's input.

The functionality part has the same constraints as before, but this time, display the data as an ordered list. Make sure to handle unknown breeds.

If there is no sub-breed for a breed, show a paragraph with the text `No sub-breeds found!`

You can use the IDs we've provided to select the elements.

## Objectives

Your page should:

- Contain a `button` with the id `button-show-sub-breed` and the text `Show Sub-Breed`;
- Use the [DOG API](https://dog.ceo/dog-api/documentation);
- Display the breed's sub-breeds as a list from the API;
- Handle unknown input and show a paragraph with the text `Breed not found!`;
- Handle a case when there are no sub-breeds and show a paragraph with the text `No sub-breeds found!`

## Examples

**Example 1**: *after entering a breed name and clicking the button*

![dog glossary sub-breed list](https://ucarecdn.com/0f17e33c-1b3b-419c-af1e-9f277ca83f2c/)

**Example 2**: *after entering a breed name without a sub-breed and clicking the button*

## Description

Now that we've shown sub-breeds, let's show all breeds with the sub-breeds.

When the user clicks the new button, show all breeds as a list. You can check the API documentation for the endpoint.

Start by adding a new `button` with the id of `button-show-all` and the text `Show All Breeds`.

The functionality part has the same constraints as before, so display the data as an ordered list.

Also, if there is a sub-breed for a breed, show the sub-breeds as an unordered list inside the list item.

You can use the IDs we've provided to select the elements.

## Objectives

Your page should:

- Contain a button with the ID `button-show-all` and the text `Show All Breeds`;
- Use the [DOG API](https://dog.ceo/dog-api/documentation);
- Display all breeds as an ordered list and sub-breeds as a nested unordered list from the API.

## Example

**Example 1**: *after clicking the button.*

![dog glossary all breeds list](https://ucarecdn.com/8cbebebc-b4cb-4aac-9d37-e551c2281173/)
